historicalReferences: Mario Andretti's win in 1978 – a true American hero winning at an American classic. What a moment!
The United States Grand Prix at Watkins Glen was a staple of the Formula 1 calendar for two decades, creating countless iconic moments.
The tragic 1973 race saw Francois Cevert lose his life, a dark day forever etched in Watkins Glen's history.
In 1975, Niki Lauda secured his first Formula 1 World Championship at Watkins Glen, a pivotal moment in his legendary career.
The Can-Am era at Watkins Glen was a golden age of motorsport, with legendary drivers and machines battling it out on this very circuit.
Names like Hill, Clark, and Stewart all conquered Watkins Glen in the early days of Formula 1 here.
The Glen has seen everything from sports car endurance races to NASCAR showdowns, each adding another layer to its rich heritage.
1961 saw the first US Grand Prix held at Watkins Glen, marking the beginning of a long and storied relationship between the track and Formula 1.
The 1971 US Grand Prix, with Francois Cevert taking his first and only F1 win, a bittersweet memory for the Tyrrell team.
Many legendary battles have unfolded here at The Glen, solidifying its status as a true test of driver and machine.

strategyPoints: Tire degradation is always a concern here at Watkins Glen, especially in the Carousel and the Boot. Managing those tires will be key.
The pit lane here isn't particularly long, meaning the pit stop loss time is relatively low, making multiple stop strategies viable.
Fuel consumption is relatively high around this 5.43km layout, requiring careful fuel management throughout the race.
The length of the Grand Prix circuit at Watkins Glen means that strategic gambles can pay off, but only if executed perfectly.
A safety car period at the wrong time can completely ruin a team's strategy. It's a real roll of the dice here.
With several high-speed corners, getting the aero balance right is crucial for both qualifying and race pace.
The undercut can be very powerful here, so expect to see teams trying to gain track position by pitting early.
Warmer temperatures will likely lead to increased tire wear, forcing teams to adapt their strategies on the fly.
weatherCommentary: The weather in the Finger Lakes region can be unpredictable. We've seen sunshine, rain, and even fog all in the same day here at Watkins Glen.
Keep an eye on those clouds gathering over Seneca Lake; a sudden downpour could change everything.
The wind can be a factor here, particularly on the long straights, affecting the car's stability.
The humidity is rising, which will make conditions even tougher on the drivers, especially inside the cockpit.
That sunshine is beating down on the track, pushing the track temperatures higher and higher. Tire management will be critical.
